sections.content: A before-and-after policy shift is a natural home for passive voice: offices were sold, then a policy was transformed, access was restricted, posts were reserved. The institution or the practice stays the subject across the whole narrative. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Muchos cargos administrativos fueron literalmente vendidos por la corona española.
items.english: Many administrative posts were literally sold by the Spanish crown.

items.spanish: Esa situación fue transformada radicalmente por las reformas borbónicas.
items.english: That situation was radically transformed by the Bourbon reforms.

items.spanish: La venta de cargos fue restringida drásticamente.
items.english: The sale of posts was drastically restricted.

items.spanish: Los puestos más importantes fueron reservados casi exclusivamente para peninsulares recién llegados.
items.english: The most important posts were reserved almost exclusively for newly arrived peninsulares.

sections.content: A paragraph tracing a policy reversal often needs exactly this shape: fue vendido (what used to happen) → fue transformada (the turning point) → fue restringida / fueron reservados (the new reality). Passive voice keeps the reader's attention on the practice itself changing, not on the individual officials carrying it out.
